propositions: The shell guard '[ -f <path> ] || { echo "change predates the gate" — skipping; exit 0; }' appears 24 times across six workflow files with copies drifting apart, causing missed guards (anxious-resistant-urson) and unguarded steps (sapphire-vulnerable-fruitfly).

A shared implementation (composite action, helper module) cannot serve the guard because it lives in the repo and is absent on pre-gate trees, making it impossible to mechanically replace the inline guards.
The guard is applied unevenly: test.yml invokes check_readme_quickstart.py and probe_rebar.py without guards while gerrit-verify.yaml guards the same scripts.

Four sites carry behaviour that a bare guard skip would silently drop: mutation.yml writes GITHUB_OUTPUT on skip, optionality.yml guards two independent generators, build-and-test.yml uses inverted conditional form, and build-and-test.yml:377 guards a data file and continues into a command that can fail.
Every gate step must either carry an -f guard for its required file or a mandatory-reason # predates-gate-ok: marker, enforced by completeness test.
Every guarded step body must exit 0 and print the canonical message when run in an empty directory, enforced by empty-tree behaviour test.
